reply.reply: RAM is short for Random Access Memory — it's the temporary storage that your computer uses to quickly access and process data while running programs. Think of it like a workspace: when you're working on a document or playing a game, the data you're using is stored in RAM so your computer can access it fast. It's volatile, meaning it loses all data when the power is turned off.
